title: JSW MG Motor India To Invest Rs 3,500 Crore To Double Halol Plant Capacity To 2.2 Lakh Vehicles By January 2028
text:
Business
Swarajya Staff
Aug 27, 2026 | Updated 09:57 AM GMT+5:30

JSW MG Motor India plans to invest Rs 3,500 crore to double production capacity at its Halol plant in Gujarat to 2.2 lakh vehicles annually by January 2028.
The joint venture between JSW Group and China's SAIC Motor expects to surpass 95,000 vehicles in calendar year 2026 and target the 100,000-unit milestone, up from approximately 70,500 vehicles in 2025.
The automotive manufacturer currently operates at a capacity of around 110,000 units annually at its Halol facility.
This capacity will increase to 160,000 units by March 2027 before reaching the full 220,000-unit target by early 2028.
The company's vendors are contributing an additional Rs 2,500 crore to the expansion, bringing the broader investment to approximately Rs 6,000 crore.
Parth Jindal, director of JSW MG Motor India, confirmed that the Halol plant could eventually accommodate production of around 400,000 vehicles annually without requiring a new location for at least the next three to four years. The capacity expansion forms part of the company's strategy to grow volumes by 35-40 per cent annually whilst strengthening its position in India's new-energy vehicle segment.
The expansion comes as JSW MG Motor focuses heavily on electric vehicles and plug-in hybrids, with new-energy vehicles accounting for over 80 per cent of total sales in recent months.
The company has launched the Hector Tomahawk on its newly developed ADAPT platform, which supports multiple new-energy powertrains including electric, hybrid, and plug-in hybrid technologies.
JSW Group currently owns 35 per cent of the venture, while SAIC Motor holds 49 per cent, with the remaining stake held by Indian investors, dealers, and employees.
